title: Finite gluing of graded-module charts
statement: Let $S$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring with grading $\mathcal A$, and $M$ a $\mathbb Z$-graded $S$-module with internal grading $\mathcal M$ compatible with scalar multiplication. Set $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj]. Index charts by pairs $f=(a,d)$ with $d>0$ and $a\in S_d$, put $D_f=D_+(a)$, $R_f=S_{(a)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and let $Z_f$ be submodules of $M_a$ whose carriers are precisely the equal-degree fractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Suppose additive maps $\rho_{f,g}:Z_f\to Z_g$ and ring maps $\rho^S_{f,g}:R_f\to R_g$ are given for every $D_g\subseteq D_f$. Suppose each inclusion admits a homogeneous relation $g^e=bf$ with $e>0$, each $\rho$ is semilinear over $\rho^S$, and for every such relation it sends $y/f^m$ to $b^my/g^{em}$. Assume identities, composition and bijectivity when chart opens coincide. Assume moreover every ring restriction is induced by a ring map $S_f\to S_g$ commuting with $S$. For every finite cover $D_f=\bigcup_iD_{g_i}$ and elements $q_i\in Z_{g_i}$ agreeing after restriction to the product chart $g_ig_j$, there exists a unique $t\in Z_f$ restricting to all $q_i$. The empty cover is included.

proof.text: Apply gradedModuleAwayRestriction. Its submodules equal the given Z by extensionality of their degreeZeroFractions carriers. Represent each element of Z_f by an ordinary localized fraction and use the two fraction formulas to identify the given rho with the constructed restriction. No comparison of rhoS is needed.

Use the value formula for U(f,g) to identify it with g^deg(f)/f^deg(g). Injectivity of homogeneous localization into ordinary localization, multiplication of fractions, and pow_add prove U(f,gh)=U(f,g)*U(f,h). Apply the finite-cover clause of standardOpenProperties to obtain Ideal.span(range U(f,g_i))=top, including the empty cover.

Pull q_i back along theta(f,g_i) to s_i. For each product chart, take the two commuting squares from gradedModuleAwayRestriction and transport their common target using U(f,g_i*g_j)=U(f,g_i)*U(f,g_j). Uniqueness of kappa identifies both maps with the canonical IsLocalizedModule.lift maps of coverModuleExact, because these maps all send x/1 to x/1. Injectivity of the common comparison equivalence and the given overlap equality imply compatibility of the s_i.

Apply coverModuleExact to R_f, Z_f and the generators U(f,g_i). Its unique x localizes to s_i. Applying theta(f,g_i) and its formula on x/1 proves rho(f,g_i)(x)=q_i. Conversely, injectivity of theta(f,g_i) turns any other solution into the same localization equations, so uniqueness in coverModuleExact proves it equals x. The same proof handles n=0 without selecting an index.
